environment.cpu_throttling: Unavailable in the advertised CUA capabilities; no throttling applied
environment.server: Local Python HTTP server, no external data requests
environment.data: 1,825 records from the local cached canonical iNaturalist/eBird inventory; 10,000-row fixture repeats those records

method.comparison: Same cached inventory, compact table markup and CSS; baseline uses the previous controller via --controller-ref. Candidate includes the final mobile select max-width wrapper classes, which do not change the desktop table layout.
method.paint_opportunity_ms: Elapsed time from input dispatch through two requestAnimationFrame callbacks; permits an intervening paint, but is not a direct paint timestamp or field INP
method.initialization_ms: One observation around the controller script, excluding HTML parsing
method.dom_content_loaded_ms: One navigation timing observation; includes local loading and parsing and is not a statistically controlled load metric
method.live_dom: Attached .ll-row and element counts after the final cleared query; detached rows remain retained in memory

limits: Desktop surrogate only, not a physical or emulated slow-phone performance result.
Synthetic input dispatch excludes real input queueing delay; these numbers are not INP scores.
A single paired run per size, with shared-machine load and frame cadence affecting timing; no confidence intervals claimed.
All inventory rows still arrive as HTML and are parsed and retained. Pagination bounds attached DOM/layout and interaction work, not initial transfer, parsing, or total retained memory.
The 10,000-row candidate had slower initialization and DOMContentLoaded than baseline; no initial-load speedup is claimed.

Native browser Find searches the attached page with JavaScript enabled; the labeled species search covers all records. Full SSR remains available without JavaScript, and a complete fingerprinted CSV is linked.
The cached 1,825-record snapshot is older than the live site; the scaling fixture is not a claim of 10,000 property species.
